app.name: Press language analysis
app.tagline: Points at fragments of headlines and leads where the model recognised a language technique. It does not judge publishers or truthfulness.

feed.heading: Latest
feed.counted: {count, plural, =0 {nothing reported} one {# finding} other {# findings}}

detail.title: Headline
detail.nothingReported: The model reported no fragment here. That is an absence of a finding, not a certificate of neutrality.
detail.neutralAlternative: Without the loading it could read:
detail.openSource: Open the article at the publisher
detail.checkSource: check this fragment against the original

reliability.short: Three findings in five can be wrong.
reliability.long: Findings are produced by a language model. Checked against 64 articles it had never seen: the underline lands on the right fragment 47% of the time, and in 42% of cases the technique named beside it is right as well. Verify every highlighted fragment against the original — that is what the link next to it is for.

provenance.generated: This analysis was generated by a model. Nobody has checked it.

account.registerExplainer: An account remembers saved articles and the categories you follow. It does not change what the analysis says — that is the same for everyone.
account.wrongCredentials: That address or password is wrong.
account.addressTaken: An account with that address already exists.
account.invalidInput: Check the address and the password length.
account.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Try again in a quarter of an hour.
account.failed: That did not work. Try again.
account.savedEmpty: You have not saved any articles yet.
account.subscriptionsExplainer: Tick the categories you care about. Nothing is sent anywhere — the choice is stored on your account.
account.deleteExplainer: Removes the account, its sessions, saved articles and followed categories. This cannot be undone.
account.exportExplainer: Downloads everything the account holds: the address, when it was created, session times, saved articles and followed categories. Without the password and without session tokens — those are credentials, not data.

ops.heading: Operator panel
ops.explainer: Diagnostics for the model and the pipeline. Everything here is a statement about how the analysis behaves — never about how any newsroom writes.
ops.someFailing: {count, plural, one {# check is failing} other {# checks are failing}}.
ops.promptVersionsWhy: More than one row means the feed is showing analyses that cannot be compared with each other.
ops.driftWhy: A rising `quotes_rejected` is the quote validator doing its job. A rise means the model drifted, the prompt changed, or an ingest change altered the text the offsets are measured against.
